key_insight: Activation probes that work on short-context inputs often fail when deployed on long-context, production distributions; with targeted architectural and training changes, probes can be made to generalize across this shift.
problem_solved: Bridging the generalization gap of activation-based probes when models are evaluated on longer, real-world context lengths than those seen during probe development.
method: Diagnose failure modes by measuring probe performance across short→long context shifts and isolating where representations change.
Design probe architectures and training protocols that are context-length robust (e.g., context-aware pooling, position-invariant features, and augmentation with long-context examples).
Validate on production-like distributions and iterate with regularization/ensemble strategies to reduce false negatives under long-context inputs.
impact: Makes activation probes reliable for real-world safety and misuse-detection deployments on long-context models (like Gemini), reducing missed detections and improving trustworthiness of runtime monitoring.
visual_elements: Line chart showing probe accuracy vs. input context length (steep drop without fixes, flat/robust with fixes).
Schematic of probe architecture highlighting context-aware pooling or position-invariant components.
Bar chart of generalization gap (short vs long) before and after the proposed interventions.
Pipeline diagram: training with augmented long-context data → probe model → production evaluation/monitoring loop.
paper_authors: János Kramár, Joshua Engels, Zheng Wang, Bilal Chughtai, Rohin Shah
